rooms.long: The ruins of a large city.
This is the portal room. As development continues, these areas will be removed from the portal room and linked to the full world.
A broken stone arch leans over the road, its timbers split and sagging. Crumbled masonry seals the passage, and old iron fittings lie rusted in the weeds.
The crossing is choked with gravel and dead leaves where a broad street meets a narrower lane. Fallen posts and a tilted sign hold a silence settled over long neglect.
Weathered stones mark the meeting of two old streets, their lines softened by drifted grit. A broken post leans over the junction, and no track has passed in generations.
A narrow walk runs beneath slumped beams and the last remains of a shaded trellis. Motes of dust cling to the air, and the stones are slick with old rot.
The covered path is broken here, its ribs split and scattered across the paving. Wind drifts through the gaps, stirring leaves that have gathered in the hollows.
A hollowed stretch of passage runs between damp stone walls. The roof timbers have fallen away, leaving the corridor open to dull light and slow rain.
The walkway dips into a shallow trough where stones have settled unevenly. A thin film of moss trails along the seams, and the air sits heavy with damp.
The path narrows beneath the remains of a withered canopy. Splintered slats litter the ground, and the walls are dark with rain stains and age.
A quiet stretch of stone runs west, its seams filled with grit and grass. The remnants of a low railing sag along the edge, half buried in dust.
The cover above the walk has failed, opening to a pale strip of sky. Loose stones and splintered wood lie scattered, and the ground shows long years of weathering.
A wide junction opens where several streets once met. The stones are worn smooth, and scattered rubble marks where structures have slumped into the road.
The walk widens before crumbling walls that once framed a corner of the city. Loose stone and soil have spilled over the paving, and the air hangs still.
A battered gateway stands between worn walls, its lintel cracked and sagging. Dust gathers in the deep grooves of the threshold, and no sound follows the road beyond.
The road angles west through a narrowed gap between leaning stonework. Chipped blocks and pale grit mark a boundary that time has left without purpose.
Westroad runs between low stone shells, their upper courses missing. Fallen blocks lie in the ruts, and a thin growth of grass softens the road.
The road narrows into a quiet channel of stone and dust. A collapsed lintel lies across one wall, and the space beyond it is dark and empty.
Windblown grit has gathered in thin drifts along the road. The stonework is stained and pitted, and a few twisted iron bands cling to the wall.
A long crack splits the paving, running the length of the road. The break is filled with rubble and silt, and the surrounding stones are polished dull by time.
The road turns beside a wall of dark basalt blocks, their faces chipped and rough. A scatter of broken stone marks where another street has slumped away.
The western gate has collapsed into a heap of stone and splintered wood. Rusted fittings lie half buried, and the blocked passage holds a deep, unmoving quiet.
Basalt paving runs between dark stone walls, the joints split by weeds and grit. A low drift of broken tile lies where slow runoff has carved shallow channels.
The avenue narrows here, basalt stones dulled to slate by grit and weather. Rust-stained runoff traces the gutter, and a fallen lintel lies along the wall.
Two worn streets cross on uneven basalt, their corners softened by age and grit. The stones are cracked and slumped, leaving shallow puddles and windblown grit.
Basalt blocks crowd the street, their faces chipped and dark with thick soot. Doorways gape into shadow, and the avenue is filmed with fine dust and leaf rot.
The avenue bends around sagging walls, the basalt setts uneven and underfoot. Moss clings in the seams, and broken steps lead into silent, collapsed doorways.
A wider crossing opens where the paving is deeply scored by cart ruts and rain. The basalt is cracked into plates, and iron rings lie rusted into the stones.
Basalt Avenue runs between low facades, their lintels split and worn with age. Thin grass pushes through the cracks, and loose stones have slid into the road.
The avenue slopes toward the river quarter, the basalt slick with old stains. A scatter of masonry narrows the passage, leaving the street choked and quiet.
Cracked basalt paving meets the river road, its stones slick with old stains. A collapsed wall spills rubble into the corner, and weeds root in the gaps.
The westward river road is split by frost and root, the stones heaved uneven. A dry gutter runs alongside, packed with silt and curled leaves.
Moss clings to the low curb here, and the road narrows between leaning facades. Rusted rings jut from the masonry, their purpose long gone.
Flat stones lie loose underfoot, some tipped into a shallow rut. A broken lintel rests against a wall, half buried in grit.
The river road bends past a slumped doorway, its threshold choked with debris. Pale lichen maps the stone, and no tracks disturb the dust.
A line of cracked flagstones stretches west, fractured by roots. A low parapet crumbles toward a silent channel, its edge washed bare.
Weeds crowd the seams of the paving, softening the road into a green ribbon. The air is damp and still along the empty course.
Here the stones are stained dark, as if by old floods that never returned. A toppled iron post lies in the gutter, rusted through.
Two dead roads cross in a scatter of broken cobbles. A fractured drain grate sits at the center, packed with mud and leaves.
The southern main road is rutted and split, its stones tipped at odd angles. A fallen signboard lies half buried in dust.
A broad stretch of paving runs north and south, worn smooth in places. The bases of old walls sit empty, their timbers long gone.
Thin weeds stripe the main road here, forcing a crooked path. A low curb has crumbled into the street, leaving a scatter of chips.
The road dips slightly, holding a thin skin of damp grit. A sagging doorway yawns nearby, black with soot.
Broken cobbles gather near a collapsed stoop. The main road is silent, its centerline marked by a shallow rut.
The southern road narrows between leaning walls. Loose slate and tile litter the paving.
Old cart ruts cut through the stones, softened by moss. A toppled beam rests across the gutter.
The paving stones here are splintered and slick with lichen. Dust lies thick against the bases of the walls.
The northward main road rises slightly, its stones pale and chipped. A cold breeze funnels through the gap between empty facades.
Here the main road is flanked by crumbling foundations. A patch of nettles spills across the center line.
The stones are cracked into a ragged mosaic, some sunk low. A rusted hinge hangs from a doorframe, unmoving.
A narrow strip of sky opens above the north road, framed by broken rooflines. Shattered brick and mortar gather in drifts.
The road passes a doorway choked with rubble and ivy. Small pools of rain-dark water stain the stones.
The north road levels out and grows quiet, its surface scabbed with grit. A cracked iron grate lies in the gutter.
Two streets cross in a square of uneven stone. The corners are piled with broken masonry and grit.
The main road bends toward the gate, its stones worn thin and pale. A line of old posts leans toward the center.
The crossing is wide and empty, marked by worn paving and shallow ruts. A broken curb rings the corner where the streets meet.
A split stone arch leans over a scatter of fallen gate timbers and rusted iron. Deep grooves where a portcullis once slid are choked with mildew and windblown grit.
The road ends against the inner wall, where the paving breaks into rubble and a shallow drift of sand. The wall looms close, its lower stones stained dark by old runoff and moss.
The wall runs north and south beside a straight stretch of empty road, its cobbles split by weeds and grit. The silence here is only broken by a faint, steady draft along the stone.
A broad road runs north and south, its surface worn into shallow ruts that hold dust and rain marks. Collapsed storefronts sag along the edges, their doorways open to the air.
The road narrows between low heaps of stone, the old curbs almost buried under grit and grass. A tilted signboard rests against a wall, its paint long gone.
A stretch of broken cobbles continues through the husks of old shops, their beams exposed to sky. Weeds knot in the joints where carts once passed.
The road dips slightly, collecting a shallow sheen of silt from past rains. Cracked thresholds line both sides, leading into roofless interiors.
A faint crown in the road has collapsed, leaving a long trough filled with grit and windblown leaves. The surrounding walls are scarred with old smoke stains.
The paving is patched with mismatched stones, as if repairs once stalled here. A low mound of rubble spills from the west, half blocking the way before the crossing.
Two streets meet in a spread of fractured stone, their lines still clear beneath the dust. A collapsed corner wall exposes a dark room open to the weather.
The road straightens and grows bare, its center rutted by the ghost of old traffic. A broken post leans beside a gap where a shopfront has collapsed.
The crossing sits in the shadow of the inner wall, where the road turns and the stones are slick with old runoff. A gutter cuts across the paving and disappears into rubble.
The lane hugs the inner wall, its cobbles cracked and uneven beneath drifts of grit. Moss climbs the cold stone blocks, and a broken drainage channel runs dark and still.
A narrow run of cobbles skirts the wall, sunk and slick with damp. The high masonry is stained with mildew, and fallen stones crowd the edge of the path.
Cobbles press against the wall here, split by frost and buckling in the soil. Weeds and dark lichen gather where the stonework weeps, muting any echo.
The wall looms close over a cramped passage of worn stone, the gaps filled with dust. Rusty brackets jut from the masonry, and the air carries the chill of old damp.
The lane runs east and west between silent foundations, their doorways collapsed into piles of brick and slate. A brittle vine clings to the mortar seams.
Broken lintels and scattered tiles mark the edges of the way. Shadows pool in the empty frames of doorways, and loose plaster has long turned to dust.
The way widens a little, its stones cracked in a shallow fan where a side street meets from the north. The remains of a low wall trail off into weeds.
Fragments of carved stone lie half-buried along the edges of the lane, their markings softened by time. A faint ridge of sand has collected against the eastern curb.
The paving here is uneven, with gaps where stones have been pulled free or sunk. A narrow passage to the south is choked with grit and a slow spread of grass.
The way crosses another street in a small square of worn stone. Old foundations crowd the corners, their rooms open and empty. Wind moves freely through the gaps.
A long row of broken pillars lines the north side of the way, each stump dark with weathering. The ground is littered with slate chips and fine dust.
The lane ends at a wider crossing, its stones paling where sunlight reaches in. A toppled capstone rests near the curb, half sunk in silt.
The way is reduced to uneven slabs, their edges rounded and split by long neglect. Silt and mildew pool in the seams, and the path fades into quiet stonework to either side.
The street straightens here, hemmed by sagging fronts and shutterless frames. A line of rust runs along the gutter, and thin weeds take the joints slowly.
Wind funnels along the empty way, lifting grit across pale weathered basalt. Collapsed beams rest against a wall, leaving the road half blocked in places.
The paving breaks into small islands, the gaps filled with dark soil and rot. The street narrows toward a wider crossing ahead, where the stones dip slightly.
A worn way meets the broader boulevard on a patch of sunken stone and grit here. The junction is scarred by ruts and hollows, with grit swept into the corners.

The old paving has slumped into a shallow trough, stones split and slick with moss. Dust and leaf mold blanket the centerline, and rusted iron bands lie half-buried where something once hung above the road.
Broken curbstones edge a long, silent way, their faces dark with mildew and rain stain. A scatter of toppled posts and empty brackets hints at old markers now swallowed by grit.
Two worn ways meet in a sagging cross, their seams packed with damp grit and tiny weeds. The center stones are polished hollow by long-forgotten traffic, with rust flakes gathered in the low joints.
A narrow run of stone drifts westward, the joints packed with gray silt and moss. A bent iron frame clings to one wall, as if a bell or lantern once marked the passage.
The paving narrows here, uneven and chipped, with damp dust clotted along the edges. Empty brackets jut from the masonry overhead, their purpose lost to the quiet.
The street has sagged and cracked, letting patches of weeds break through the seams. A fallen crossbeam lies against the wall, its fittings scarred as if something once hung there and rang.
Loose stone chips blanket the ground, and the walls carry streaks of water rot and mildew. A line of small iron mounts runs along the lintel, hints of old bells or lamps now gone.
The eastern stretch runs straight and hollow, its stones slick with moss. A low wall beside it is buckled and split.
Silt lies in shallow drifts along the edge of the road. A fallen shutter leans against the stone, water-dark and warped.
Patches of grass push through the joints in the paving here. The river channel beside the road is choked with debris and still.
The road narrows between blank fronts, their doors hanging askew. Wind has swept the stones clean in thin streaks.
A shallow rut marks the center line, worn deep before the silence. Small piles of gravel gather against the curb.
Cracked stones and broken mortar leave the road ragged. A rusted chain lies half sunk in the silt.
The road ends at a tumbled edge of stone, dropping to a dry, weeded bank. Broken posts stand like stumps along the rim.
The crossing is a scatter of worn stones, their edges smoothed by time. The two ways meet in silence, framed by damp, crumbling walls.
The way thins into broken stones, the once- straight line sagging. Fallen trim and damp rubble gather at the end of the road.
Wide paving slabs lie buckled and parted by grass. A line of soot-streaked stone posts leans in slow collapse.
The way runs quiet between squat walls, its stones dulled and uneven. Old carvings are worn to nubs, nearly erased by weather.
A shallow channel cuts along the path, filled with grit and broken tile. The air is cool and still between the close walls.
The paving here is split by roots, forming a jagged seam. A toppled arch stone blocks part of the way.
Loose stones crunch under a thin coat of dust. A rusted bracket clings to the wall, its mate long gone.
The street opens slightly, revealing pale stone flecked with lichen. A shallow depression holds rain-dark stains.
The way ends beneath a sagging lintel, the stones split and bowed. A scatter of fallen blocks marks the threshold into the north.
A long counter sags under its own weight, split and furred with dust. Behind it, shelves lie in heaps, and the air is stale and still.

Rot-softened beams sag over a long counter gone gray with dust and mildew. Benches lie broken in the hush, and a sour stain clings where drink once spilled. The hearth is cold, its iron hooks rusted and half-buried in grit.
Stall frames lean inward, their rails splintered and gray. Dry straw rot and scattered nails litter the floor.
A heavy door hangs askew on broken hinges, opening into a chamber choked with rubble. Iron bands are rusted through, and the floor has sunk into a shallow pit.
Soot-dark stone surrounds a dead hearth, its ash long blown away. Crumbling brick and damp stains mark the still chamber.
Stone paths fracture beneath a mat of low weeds and windblown soil. A dry fountain bowl sits cracked and empty under leaning trees.
Thick grass swallows old benches, leaving warped planks and rusted bolts. A sagging iron fence lists inward, half-buried in leaf mold.
A wide clearing lies mute, its stones scattered and moss-dark. Birdless branches arch over the space, their shadows unmoving.
A once-open lawn is now a tangle of thorn and nettle. Broken edging stones ring the growth like a half-lost border.
Dry shrubs crowd a cracked path, and pale trunks stand stripped of bark. Old lantern hooks hang crooked from a low wall, black with rust.
The ground dips where a pond once spread, now a dish of silt and weeds. Scattered paving stones and toppled posts mark the forgotten walkway.
Rust flakes from a split rack, and the floor is filmed with dust and old grit. A warped counter and dull iron hooks suggest where blades once hung, now left to mildew and silence.
Rot-softened padding slumps in a heap, and dust clogs the seams of a collapsed frame. A few dull buckles and a cracked mannequin hint at fittings once done here, now lost to mildew.
Soot clings to the stone, and rusted hooks hang in a silence of dust and mildew. Rotting tubs and ash-stained gutters hint at preserved fare in long-neglected ruin.
A cracked lathe stands in the corner, silent and ruined beneath dust and mildew. Spilled shavings and dulled tools sit in rot, hinting at careful turning left to waste.

Narrow shelves sag under warped boxes and tarnished curios, all buried in dust. The air is sweet with mildew, and the floorboards have bowed around a collapsed display case. A cracked mirror leans in back, its gilt peeling away.

Soot stains the stone around a slumped hearth, and chalky rings fade on the floor beneath a crust of dust. Shelves of warped wood hold scattered vials and stiffened pages, their ink bled by damp and mildew.

A narrow stair ends in a loft where a worktable sits split and furred with mildew. Blackened candle stubs and cracked lenses lie in drifts of dust, hinting at old study now drowned in silence and rot.

The low room smells of damp stone, its beams soft with rot and its floor hidden beneath dust. A simple table has collapsed beside a cold hearth, and a notched post stands where some small training once took place.
Broken molds and a rusted frame lie in silent dust, the shop in ruin. Rot and mildew stain the stone, hinting at chimes once shaped here in neglect.
Hardened wax pools on a sagging table, silent beneath dust and mildew. Empty molds and a stale tallow smell linger in rot, hinting at candlework long abandoned.
A copper coil lies split on the floor, silent and wrecked under dust and mildew. Dry barrels and a stained hearth sit in rot, hinting at spirits once made here and long forgotten.
A wide threshold of cracked stone leads into a cavernous hall, its pillars pocked and green with mildew. Shattered bowls lie at the base of a raised dais, and ash-dark banners hang in ragged silence.

Tall columns loom over a nave littered with fallen tiles and windblown dust. A cracked altar slab sits beneath a roof opened to rain, and the air carries mildew from sodden tapestries curled against the walls.
Stone benches sit in crooked rows, their edges rounded by damp and rot. A shallow brazier lies overturned near the front, its iron scaled with rust and its embers long gone.
A side chamber is lined with niche shelves, now empty and gray with dust. Wax drips have hardened on the floor, their puddles greened by mildew and tracked with grit from a door that no longer shuts.
A narrow gallery runs above the main hall, its railings split and softened by rot. Torn cloth once bright hangs in strips, and the air is still but for the dry rattle of loose tiles.

A low stone chamber lies open to weather, its floor thick with dust and mildew, with drips tracing the walls where plaster once held. Rust-tormented bars sag above a cracked counter, and a warped slot in the wall still hints at where coins once passed.
A warped board is riddled with rusted nails, silent under dust and mildew. Faded names and tally marks sit in rot, hinting at claims once posted in a long-quiet hall.
A tight passage runs between leaning walls, choked with damp rot and black mildew. Broken drains and sagging lintels suggest a service way once kept clear, now sealed in silence.
The room is silent under a crust of paper dust, with broken rollers and a sagging frame. Ink stains still darken the boards, and warped trays rot in the damp.
Cold ash and rusted tools lie scattered across a cracked stone floor. A collapsed bellows and a soot-blackened hearth hint at heat that has not lived here for centuries.
This narrow cut between walls is choked with grit and damp rot. Mildew climbs the stones, and a broken crate hints at rough dealings that once hid here.
The nave stands in silence, its benches split and furred with mildew. A broken basin and a faded sigil suggest solace once offered here, now left to dust.
Dust lies thick over a ring of cracked tiles, and the air tastes of damp stone. Chipped shelves and a tarnished inlay hint at study and rite, now abandoned.
Desks sit in crooked ranks, their drawers swollen and stuck with damp. Mold frets at the corners of scattered ledgers, and a rusted seal lies half buried in dust where clerks once tallied.

A soot-black kiln squats against the wall, its mouth choked with ash and dust. Fused beads and curled shards glitter faintly amid rot and mildew, and a workbench has split under the weight of silence.
Practice posts lean at odd angles, their tops splintered and gray with rot. Racks of rusted gear line the walls, and dust has buried the scuffed floor where drills once rang.
Soot smears the walls above a narrow counter, and empty hooks line the back. A crust of old oil darkens the floorboards, now gritty with dust and ash.

Rotted timbers sag above a cramped room, the floor buried in grit and splintered boards. Rust-flecked hooks and a few warped racks cling to the walls, hinting at what once lined them. A stale hush and mildew settle over the hollow space.
A narrow bedframe sags against the wall, its straw long moldered into dust. A cracked chest sits open, and a single practice rail leans nearby, dulled by mildew and time.

A sunken patch of earth lies between low foundations, its surface matted with weed, dust, and black mildew. Rotted post stubs and a bent iron bracket linger at the edge, with scattered planks and a worn stone lip hinting at some former frontage.
Low foundations ring a vacant patch, silent beneath dust, mildew, and rot. A broken sign frame hints at trade, the lot left to crumble.
A low hall of stone desks and alcoves sits gutted and still. Mildew darkens the plaster, and empty niches line the walls where records once rested.
The alley narrows to a blind wall, its cobbles slick with grime and decay. Rotten beams lean overhead, and a stale dampness pools where the light dies.
Scuffed boards and long tables fill a wide room, now gray with dust. Faded tally marks and peg holes linger on the walls, hinting at lessons once kept here.
A small room with a low counter sits abandoned, its shelves stripped clean. The air is stale with rot, and broken pegs show where trade once hung.
Rows of low frames line the walls, their slats warped and gray with dust. Mildew softens the plaster, and the floor is worn smooth by vanished footsteps.
A narrow storefront opens to a room of bare shelves and a sagging counter. Dust heaps in the corners, and a faded sign fragment clings to the lintel.
A cracked counter stretches across the room, with empty racks behind it. Rot has crept into the floorboards, and mildew stains blur whatever goods once stood here.
A broad patch of bare earth interrupts the street, rimmed by broken foundations. Splintered posts and sunken stones hint at a lost structure beneath the weeds.
A tight room of empty pallets sits in silence, the straw long gone. Rot has crept up the posts, and the air is stale with old sweat and mildew.
Narrow sleeping frames stand in two lines, stripped to bare wood and cobweb. A boarded alcove gapes at the far end, and the boards sag with damp.
A long chamber holds only the outline of former sleeping spaces, now dusted gray. Moisture streaks the walls, and the floorboards creak under a film of grit.
The room is divided by low rails where thin beds once rested in rows. Mildew and rot soften the timbers, and the air lies flat and stale.
Warped wooden frames cling to the walls, their joints loose and splintered. Cobwebs gather in the corners, and a sour dampness hangs over the floor.
A cramped chamber shows the shadow of old sleeping rows in the dust. Plaster has fallen in sheets, and the boards are dark with mildew.
Low bed frames run along the sides, stripped to bare ribs and powdery with dust. The ceiling sags, and the stale air holds the hint of old bedding.
Long lines of empty sleeping frames sit rigid in the gloom, their wood soft with rot. The floor is pitted and damp, and silence presses against the walls.
A hinged span lies open over the gap, its timbers split and softened by rot. Rusty chains sag from the ruined fittings, and the stone landing is scoured bare.
Two battered towers hem in this passage, their upper floors cracked and open to the sky. Loose stones and damp rubble gather where a wooden span once steadied the gap.
The gap between the towers narrows here, with soot-dark stone and warped iron bands clinging to the walls. The floor is littered with crumbling mortar and a rot-stained beam that once barred the way.
A wide paved court lies quiet, its cobbles sunken and furred with mildew. Old drain lines and a broken curb hint at orderly traffic long gone.
Dust drifts along the open court, pooling against slumped walls and empty doorways. The stones are worn smooth in a broad path, the track of forgotten patrols.
Silence hangs in this inner court where weeds thread between cracked stones. A low step and a cracked curb trace where carts once turned.
A low chamber opens off the court, with arrow slits clogged by rot and mildew. An overturned bench and a rusted hook speak of watchers gone.
These steps descend into damp shadow, their edges rounded and slick with moss. A crumbling handrail line and iron pegs show where the stair was once kept tight.
The stairwell turns here, crowded by damp stone and a fractured landing. Dust cakes the treads, and a broken sconce hints at night watches that ended long ago.
A long narrow room holds the remains of low platforms, their frames rotted and collapsed. The air is stale with old mildew, and a strip of wall hooks suggests ordered kit.
The upper steps rise into a roofless shaft where rain darkens the stone. Loose grit and rust flakes collect along the wall where a rail once ran.
This lofty chamber opens to the wind, its outer wall cracked and partly fallen away. A ring of worn stone at the edge hints at a place of watch and signal.
The court widens toward a collapsed corner, its paving buckled and wet with seepage. A half-ruined post and iron ring suggest where orders and notices once hung.
Cold stone surrounds this open court, with mildew streaks and fallen chips whitening the ground. A shallow channel in the paving runs toward a broken drain, a remnant of tidy upkeep.
The court here is narrower, hemmed by rough walls and roofless alcoves. A rusted bracket and a shallow socket in the stone hint at a former lantern line.
Gray dust coats the paving, and fragments of plaster lie in soft ridges. A broad, straight run of stones implies an old processional path through the ward.
A circular stone shaft yawns in the floor, its lip chipped and stained with lime. The old windlass is gone, leaving only rusted bolts and a stale breath of damp below.
Splintered stall walls lean inward, their rails slick with mildew. A cracked feeding trough sits dry, and dust lies thick where hooves once churned.
A broad stone hearth squats in the center, dark with soot and long without heat. An anvil stump and iron tools sit rusted among cinders and damp ash.
Low shelves and bins crowd the room, warped and split from damp. Cinder stains and rusted nail heads hint at the forge work once stacked here.
Rusty ring bolts stud the posts, and the plank walls bow with age. Old straw dust clings to the floor, mixed with a sour, damp rot.
Crooked hooks line the wall, empty but scarred by long use. The boards are warped and blackened with damp, and the air is still and rank.
A narrow run between stalls is choked with silt and crumbled wood. The rails are split, and the stone base is slick with moss.
A stone trough is split down the middle, its basin crusted with lime. Rot has eaten the surrounding planks, leaving gaps filled with dust and mold.
Low pen walls barely stand, their joints loose and sagging. Mildew freckles the timbers, and a damp chill clings to the floor.
A collapsed loft hangs above, its beams broken and draped in cobwebs. Dry chaff dust coats the ground, now darkened by years of damp.
Stall partitions linger as gray ribs, and rusted hinges hang from them. The floor is packed hard and bare, with only the stink of wet rot left.
A shallow trough sits in a drained corner, its stones green with mildew and grit. Cracked channels run toward a blocked grate, suggesting long-abandoned care for animals.
A row of bays opens along the wall, their gates missing and frames twisted. Water stains creep up the stone base, and the air is heavy with mildew.
A low loft space is sunk and split, its ladder gone. Mold spreads across the rafters, and a dull dampness fills the room.
Bare racks line one side, warped and splintered by time. Rust flakes from old fittings, and dust gathers in soft drifts.
Split rails mark the stall lines, some fallen flat into the dirt. The ground is rutted and cold, with a sour odor of rot.
Pen walls stand in crooked rows, their boards gray and powdery. Cobwebs hang from the corners, and the floor is gritty with old straw dust.
Wide bays open into shadow, their frames softened by decay. Dampness beads on the stone, and the silence is thick and close.
A narrow corner holds a low block and scarred posts, now slick with mold. The surrounding boards are split, and the air is stale with wet wood.
An iron post rises from the floor, its ring eaten with rust. Chaff and dust cake the ground, and the walls weep with damp.
A line of rotted posts stands uneven, each marked by rust streaks. The floor is hard and bare, broken only by a drift of grit.
Stall floors have sunk into the earth, leaving the boards slanted and warped. Mildew climbs the posts, and a musty silence settles in the gaps.
A pen lies open and collapsed, its boards scattered and softened by rot. The stone base is stained dark, and the air hangs damp and still.
A dingy alleyway
Overgrown beds sag beneath nettles and mildew-dark leaves, their borders crumbled. A fallen trellis and a cracked basin suggest careful tending long since undone.
A low shed sags over a grated stone lip, its boards soft with rot. Mildew and silt stain the edges, hinting at a passage once kept clear below.
The alley narrows between damp walls, with soot and slime streaking the stone. Old drainage grooves and a collapsed plank hint at service traffic that no longer comes.
This tight passage ends in rubble, its floor sunk with dust and mortar. A bricked arch and iron pins suggest a once-used service door.
Soot-blackened stone closes in here, and the air is still and stale. A broken lintel and splintered frame imply a long-removed gate.
The passage bends in shadow, damp with rot and flecked with peeling lime. A shallow gutter runs along the base of the wall, a remnant of old refuse flow.
Moisture beads on the close walls, and the paving is dark with mildew. A rusted hinge stump and scored stone hint at a narrow door once kept shut.
The alley widens slightly, filled with rotting boards and a soft bed of dust. A leaning beam and iron staple suggest a former stall or screen.
The dead-end passage is choked with grit and damp cobbles, quiet under sagging walls. Faint nail holes in the stone imply shelving or a lean-to long since gone.
This crooked alley is lined with cracked stone and peeling plaster that smells of old damp. A broken curb and shallow ruts hint at steady foot and cart traffic.
Stink Alley Way
Brine has long dried into a crust, leaving the stall rank and silent. Splintered tables and a rusted hook hint at trade in flesh that has since rotted away.
The shed reeks of damp earth and rot, with sacks collapsed into dark pulp. A battered scoop and stained planks hint at soil and dung once bartered here.
A narrow room holds a cracked stone basin and a warped chair frame. Rust flakes and dust cover the floor where tools once hung in neat rows.
Torn curtains hang in tatters, and dust mats the warped floor boards. A low dais and broken screens hint at a private vice now drowned in mildew.
